register.name: Malta Government Stocks, August 2026 (3.80% 2036 and 4.25% 2046)
register.detail: Treasury · results of 10 August 2026 · 3.80% MGS 2036 (IV) due 8 July 2036 · 4.25% MGS 2046 (II) due 14 September 2046 · retail €162.7M at €100 · auction €337M · €852.2M received against €300M on issue and a €200M over-allotment option
register.note: Bid-to-cover ratio 2.84; 4,245 retail applications and auction bids; retail applications allotted in full
register.text: Two Malta Government Stocks, a ten-year and a twenty-year stock, issued by the Treasury to retail and wholesale investors. They fund the State budget as a whole; their proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Malta Government Stocks, April 2026 (3.80% 2036 and 4.10% 2041)
register.detail: Ministry for Finance · final results 5 May 2026 · 3.80% MGS 2036 (III) and 4.10% MGS 2041 (II) · retail €209.3M at €100 from 5,189 applications · auction €290M from 59 bids of €684M · €893.3M received against €300M on issue and up to €200M more
register.note: The amount adds the retail allotment of €209,305,700 and the auction allotment of €290,000,000; the release does not state a total
register.text: Two Malta Government Stocks, a ten-year and a fifteen-year stock, offered to retail investors at a fixed price and to wholesale investors by auction. They fund the State budget as a whole; their proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Malta Government Stocks issued in 2025
register.detail: Treasury · annual report 2025 · five new MGS in three issues · February €449.8M · July €388.0M · November €426.2M · consolidated central government debt €11.2bn at 31 December 2025
register.note: In the November 2025 issue, retail investors were allotted €103.2M and the auction €323.0M, across the 2.55% MGS 2030 (V), 3.40% MGS 2035 (IV) and 3.80% MGS 2040 (II), both fungible issues
register.text: The Treasury’s gross issuance of Malta Government Stocks in 2025, in three issues to retail and wholesale investors. It funds the State budget as a whole; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · financial contribution EUR 328,230,928 · plan approved 5 October 2021, amended 14 July 2023, 20 June 2025 and 12 December 2025 · amendment proposed 13 July 2026, contribution unchanged · fourth payment request of €51.5M partially approved 20 March 2026 · €18.9M paid 27 May 2026
register.note: Part of the fourth payment is withheld until milestone 6.36, a tax reform against aggressive tax planning, is fulfilled
register.text: EU funding for agreed reforms and investments under the Recovery and Resilience Facility, including a REPowerEU chapter. The fourth payment covered measures for the decarbonisation of energy and transport and for education and healthcare, among them reading programmes helping over 1,000 young students catch up, serving the education, health and energy standards.

register.name: Second electricity interconnector with Italy (IC2)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · approved 8 July 2025 · signed 23 April 2026 · promoter the Republic of Malta · 122 km, 220 kV, 225 MW subsea cable from Magħtab to Ragusa, Sicily · total cost €296.68M, of which €165.78M from the European Regional Development Fund
register.note: Scheduled to enter into operation in the first quarter of 2027; tendered and implemented by Interconnect Malta, a 100% government-owned company
register.text: An EIB loan for a second high-voltage subsea cable linking the Enemalta terminal station at Magħtab with Terna’s substation in Ragusa, running in parallel with the existing interconnector. It raises Malta’s capacity to import electricity, for security of supply, the integration of renewable energy and stable energy prices for households and businesses, serving the energy standard.

register.name: Co-financing of the EU programmes 2021–2027, first tranche
register.detail: European Investment Bank · €260M package approved · first tranche of €130M signed 13 February 2025 in Valletta with the Ministry for Finance · Malta’s national co-financing under the Cohesion Fund, ERDF, ESF, EMFAF and Just Transition Fund
register.note: The Treasury reports a new €77.85M EIB loan for EU Funds 2021–2027 disbursed in June 2025, at 3.348%, maturing 7 April 2039
register.text: EIB financing for Malta’s national share of the EU’s 2021–2027 programmes, covering health infrastructure, credit for SMEs, digital transformation, biodiversity, wastewater management and sustainable transport. It serves the health, water and livelihood standards.

items.name: Merill Rural Network
items.text: A de facto social enterprise, set up in 2010 as an ecotourism venture, that connects local farmers, breeders and artisans with quality tourism and promotes their 100% local products, giving its 30 active members and their families more sources of income; on 7 November 2025 it won the Social Impact category of the Malta Business Awards.
